title: Away from nightclubs until 1934; the tea room and the piano
summary: She stopped nightclub work after about 1927 and returned by 1934. During the Depression she and her husband ran a tea room where touring musicians played their piano.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Well, you said about 27 at Casino. Was it the next year at Panama, would you say?

Well, I tell you, after, that wasn't directly after I left the casino that I went. See, when I, after I quit there, I didn't work no more until about, in the nightclubs anymore until about, about, uh, let's see, what year was it I started back? That was 27. I didn't start back anymore until about 34, I guess.
Is that so? It was, uh, well into the depression before you, uh,

Yeah. Back in that kind of work. Yeah. Correct. By 34, cause that's, that's, uh, that's back when I went to the Panama, see, when, uh-huh. I didn't go, I didn't go directly back. I quit. And, uh, this piano, it has history behind it. Everybody that came to Chicago played on this piano. Duke, we had a little tea room around the corner when we lived around there during the depression. And, uh, Duke Ellington, Earl Hines, all the performers that came to Chicago at that time came to our place. At one time, uh, some colored fellow friend of ours brought a part of Dan Garber's orchestra out. He and, see, we'd serve chicken and steaks. Oh, yeah. And, of course, the gin on the side, you know. So, uh-
This was the place on Indiana Avenue?
No. When we lived at 4607 Prairie in our house.

In our house. And we, this piano, my husband says, it's too bad that we didn't have, get all the autographs from the, from the famous people that played on this piano. It's still good, and it's 33 years old. And, uh- Do you play yourself? No, I don't. I, I used to play a lot, but I had an accident on a glass door.

Cut, all my leaders was cut on a glass door, even to the sun. Yeah. So, I lost the execution, you know. Right now. I can't execute. Uh-huh. But I can just pick it out enough to, uh, learn my songs. I can learn my songs. I don't have to have nobody teach me that.
Yes, yes, the functionality. I, I see.
Uh-huh. But I used to play pretty good before that happened.
